summary: First steel fire lookout in Texas, built in 1926 at 80 ft on the Kirbyville State Forest (now E.O. Siecke State Forest); standing, but not open for public climbing.

facts.design: Steel tower, 80 feet tall, with a seven-foot-square cab

access.note: Forest open year-round during daylight hours; the tower is not available for public climbing

visit.trail_note: Forest open year-round during daylight hours; limited access by vehicle

events.note: First steel fire lookout in Texas, 80 feet, erected on the Kirbyville State Forest
Lookoutman reported 175 fires in the fall 1927 season, per a December 1927 newspaper report quoted by Forest Lookouts
Forest dedicated and renamed E.O. Siecke State Forest

notes_for_editor: Tower is on the E.O. Siecke State Forest, renamed in 1951; the record's name Kirbyville is the historic one. Record height 24.4 m matches the 80 ft given in 1926 and by TFS. A 1948 newspaper said the tower would be raised to 120 ft; no later source confirms it, and the TFS release still says 80 ft. The 1927 count (175 fires, fall 1927 season) and the TFS count (135 in the first year in use) appear to cover different periods. The 1926 and 1927 newspaper items were read only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. No current photo or condition report found; standing status rests on the FFLA list and TFS saying the tower still exists. Public climbing is not permitted per TFS.
